title: Peg loom
summary: A peg loom is a board with rows of wooden pegs, each peg holding a loop of cord. Strips of old cloth or yarn are woven round the pegs, and the finished work is slid down onto the cords in a thick, soft, hard-wearing rug. Changing the strip colour from row to row makes the pattern.
howToPlay: Pick a cloth colour from the rolls and a pattern shape from the tray.
Touch a square on the rug to weave that shape there; it is mirrored on the other half of the rug.
Copy the rug shown on the card, then press Check.
rules: The rug is mirrored left and right, so every shape you weave is also woven on its partner square.
A square counts only when its shape and its cloth colour both match the rug you are copying.
Three stars need a nearly perfect copy; you can undo or clear as often as you like.
heritageNote: Peg looms and hand-held weaving sticks are a simple, old way of making fabric, and rag rugs on peg looms are still a popular home craft because they turn worn cloth into something useful.
